about: Ways to move from one style to the next at a part boundary. Our own words. The Styles room offers them, compose.py writes them into the build prompt.

burn.name: Film burn
burn.line: The old film stalls and burns through. The new world shows behind the hole.
burn.build: Slow the outgoing picture as if the projector drags, then burn a hole that spreads from one spot (hot white core, orange rim, charred edge). The incoming style is already playing behind the hole.

rewind.name: Rewind scratch
rewind.line: The picture rewinds fast, with scratches, back into the old film.
rewind.build: Run the outgoing picture backwards for a moment with vertical scratches, jitter and a brief speed blur, then settle on the first frame of the incoming style as if the reel found its place.

iris.name: Iris
iris.line: A black circle closes on one world and opens on the next.
iris.build: Close a circular mask on the subject of the outgoing part, hold black for a few frames, then open the same circle on the incoming style.

sweep.name: Light sweep
sweep.line: A bright bar wipes across the frame and leaves the new scene.
sweep.build: Pass a soft bright bar diagonally across the frame. Everything the bar has passed is already the incoming style.

fold.name: Paper fold
fold.line: The frame folds like a page to show the next one.
fold.build: Fold the outgoing frame along a crease like a sheet of paper, with a shading gradient on the moving half, to reveal the incoming style underneath.
